svg.title: Figure B: corridor router, 273 of 273 requests decided within 30 s; 149 when native forecast coverage is required
svg.desc: Same 273 requests under two missing-input policies: 189 routes, 84 no-route proofs, 0 unresolved; and when native forecast coverage is required 35, 114, 124.
svg.text: Corridor router: 273 of 273 requests decided within 30 s; 149 when forecast coverage is required
The same 273 requests (five historical fires, reconstructed forecasts), two policies for cells where the forecast has no native value.
Missing forecast input allowed (zero-filled): the historical v8 run
189 routes · 84 model no-route proofs · 0 unresolved · slowest request 28.244 s of 30 s
Native forecast coverage required for every cell-hour a journey touches
35 routes · 114 model no-route proofs · 124 unresolved · slowest request 28.198 s of 30 s
Why: 163 of the 189 routes in the first bar occupied at least one cell-hour with no native forecast value (zero-filled), so they are
withheld when coverage is required. Absent forecast data is not proof that no route exists, so a request with no covered route and no
unrestricted no-route proof is reported unresolved (124).
Sources: research/kcf-evidence/sources/corridor-router-v8/receipts.csv (first bar: kind, wall_s, unsupported_cell_hours); research/kcf-evidence/sources/corridor-
router-v8/forecast_input_recovery/receipts.csv (second bar; reason = SUPPORT_RESTRICTED_SEARCH_NO_ROUTE for all 124 unresolved). Intermediate run on the same requests before
forecast inputs were recovered: 28 / 78 / 167 (research/kcf-evidence/sources/corridor-router-v8/support_273_receipts.csv). Evidence copied byte-for-byte from branch
codex/experimental-corridor-router-v8. Retrospective reconstructions; 30 s / 3,072 MiB guard; one Mac; run once per request; model-scoped results, not field safety.
